outcome: care utilization (attendance at comprehensive postpartum visit, postpartum depression screening, enrollment in remote hypertension monitoring, number of BP measurements)
cohort: The study included pregnant patients >32 weeks' gestation at risk for postpartum morbidity (due to intrapartum complications, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, diabetes, and/or risk factors for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders) participating in a navigation program, matched with historical controls receiving standard care.
finding: The postpartum navigation program was associated with improved rates of postpartum depression screening, continuation of breastfeeding at 6 weeks postpartum, and engagement with a remote hypertension monitoring program, despite similar attendance at comprehensive postpartum visits.
gest_age: >32 weeks' gestation for inclusion; mean gestational age at delivery was 39.0 weeks for the intervention group and 38.7 weeks for the control group.
